glossary.Iris: The coloured ring of muscle that controls the size of the pupil.
glossary.Autoimmune disease: A disease in which the immune system attacks the body's own tissues.
glossary.Sacroiliac: The joints between the sacrum and the pelvis, inflamed in ankylosing spondylitis.
glossary.Cornea: The clear front window of the eye.
glossary.Pupil: The black hole in the centre of the iris that lets light in.
glossary.Irregular pupil: A misshapen pupil, often from the iris sticking to the lens in uveitis.
glossary.Bilateral: Affecting both sides, here both eyes.
glossary.Lens capsule: The thin clear membrane surrounding the lens of the eye.
glossary.Ophthalmology: The medical specialty dealing with eye disease.
glossary.Ophthalmological emergency: An eye condition needing urgent specialist review to protect vision.
glossary.Topical corticosteroid: A steroid applied directly, here as eye drops, to reduce inflammation.
glossary.Systemic corticosteroid: A steroid given by mouth or vein, such as prednisolone, acting on the whole body.
glossary.Ciliary spasm: Painful contraction of the ciliary muscle in an inflamed eye.
glossary.Ciliary muscle: The muscle in the ciliary body that changes lens shape for focusing.
glossary.Iris sphincter: The ring muscle of the iris that constricts the pupil.
glossary.Immunosuppressant: A drug that dampens the immune system.
glossary.Genetic predisposition: An inherited tendency to develop a disease.
glossary.T-cell mediated: Driven by T lymphocytes rather than antibodies.
glossary.Angle closure glaucoma: Raised eye pressure because the drainage angle between iris and cornea is blocked.
glossary.Secondary: Caused by another condition rather than arising on its own.
glossary.Spondyloarthropathy: A family of HLA-B27 linked arthritides affecting the spine, such as ankylosing spondylitis.
glossary.CXR: Chest X-ray; here to look for hilar lymph nodes of sarcoidosis.
glossary.Slit-lamp examination: Viewing the eye with a microscope and narrow light beam to see cells in the anterior chamber.
